messages:
Rae Turner: Quick follow-up to the canary fallback RFC I want a tiny runtimeboundary: signals in, declarative rules out. Short thread.
Iris Valdez: Love the idea. What minimal fields do we need on a signal?
Rae Turner: channel, level, score, rollout_id, cohort_pct, expires_at, provenance, evidence_url. Keep compact.
Noah Kim: Local actuators must be allowed to act fast but only do reversible ops. Irreversible ops require central signed command.
Sam Holt: Add token-damper + min_dwell_seconds in policy to avoid flip-flop. Also a max_auto_rollbacks_per_day safety budget.
Rae Turner: Agreed. Signal format example (compact): channel:latency level:critical score:88 rollout:r-2026-03-21 cohort:5 expires:2026-03-21T18:00Z prov:[latency-v2] evidence:https://logs/123 seq:4521 sig:<base64>
Iris Valdez: For A/B, include impact_estimate so actuators can scale partial-diverts. Also evidence_url should link to sliced metrics.
Noah Kim: Transport: gRPC streaming preferred, signed envelope. Fallback: signed HTTP webhook for legacy infra.
Sam Holt: Flight-recorder: log raw signals + composed decision + applied action. Retention 90d. Include policy_id that triggered rule.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary started for rec-svc v2 cohort=3% at 2026-03-21T17:35Z :rocket:
Rae Turner: I'll draft a tiny proto + DSL example. Plan: shadow mode 2w, reversible actions for low-risk services, then widen. Any objections?
Iris Valdez: No objections. I'll start metric-buckets doc.
Noah Kim: I'll prototype local cache TTL and signature checks.
Sam Holt: I'll write safety-budget schema and tests for damping.
Rae Turner: Thanks team. Will link this thread from the RFC.
